sections.h2: Which selling route suits a Georgetown homeowner?
sections.html:
Georgetown owners can take a cash offer, list the house, or sell without an agent. A cash offer wins on speed and certainty, a listing on exposure, and a direct sale on cost.

The city is the Williamson County seat and, by the Census Bureau's 2022 release as the city's visitor page reports it, was the fastest-growing U.S. city above 50,000 residents. Growth means steady demand, and it also means a resale competes with many new houses. A cash buyer offers a date and a price without showings. A listing can attract buyers who want a finished, staged home.

  • Cash offer: as-is, flexible closing, little prep.
  • Listing: wider reach, more work, repair requests after inspection.
  • Direct sale: lower cost, but you manage paperwork and screening.

Faster than almost anywhere. Residents numbered 47,400 in 2010 and 67,176 in 2020, and the estimate for mid-2025 is 106,907, a 58.5 percent jump over the 2020 base.

Roughly a quarter of residents (26.2 percent) are 65 or over, 19.8 percent are under 18, and the survey counts 7,191 veterans. Many owners in that older group are considering downsizing, moving closer to family or settling an estate, which often favors a quick, low-effort sale. State tax rules for seniors and veterans matter too, and they are covered below.

The city spans 57.33 square miles of land with 1,171.7 residents per square mile at the 2020 count, so it is spread out, and the average commute runs 28.2 minutes.

sections.h2: How do Georgetown homes compare on value and ownership?
sections.html:
Owners hold most Georgetown homes, and the middle value is $429,100. The Census survey for 2020 to 2024 shows owners in 69.5 percent of occupied homes and a middle rent of $1,795.

sections.h2: Does Georgetown's historic downtown affect selling a house?
sections.html:
It can, if your house sits in or near the older neighborhoods around the Square. The city's visitor page says Georgetown has four National Register historic districts and 52 individually listed properties.

The city was founded in 1848, and its Public Square area is lined with Victorian and pre-World War I buildings, with the Williamson County Courthouse from 1911 at the center. Southwestern University, established in 1840, is also in town, and Lake Georgetown and the San Gabriel River trails are close by. Those features attract buyers who value older character homes and walkable streets.

  • Ask the city planning office whether your address is in a historic district or has design standards.
  • Tell buyers early about any exterior work you have done, with permits.
  • An investor can buy an older home as-is, without the repair list a retail buyer might send.

sections.h2: What local landmarks and amenities help a Georgetown listing?
sections.html:
Georgetown's visitor page lists features that buyers recognize: the Public Square with its shops and restaurants, the Williamson County Courthouse from 1911, and a Great American Main Street designation the city earned in 1997. Southwestern University, founded in 1840, is also in the city.

For outdoor access, the same page counts nearly nine miles of hike and bike trails along the San Gabriel River, nearly seven miles of trails in Garey Park, and 28 miles around Lake Georgetown. A house close to any of these should say so plainly in a listing or to a cash buyer, because location is part of the price.

Confirm distances yourself and avoid promising anything about school zoning or future development. Ask the school district and city planning office for current boundaries and plans.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks affect a Georgetown seller?
sections.html:
Seniors are numerous here, so these breaks come up often. School districts must exempt $140,000 of homestead value, with a further $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.

For those owners, the school tax on the homestead is generally capped at what it was the year they first qualified. The cap can follow you to a new Texas homestead in proportion, though added improvements beyond repairs can lift it. A surviving spouse who is 55 or older may keep it in some cases, and cities, counties and junior college districts may adopt their own cap.

Disabled veterans get separate exemptions that run from up to $5,000 at a 10 to 29 percent rating to up to $12,000 at 70 to 100 percent, and a full exemption on the homestead at 100 percent disabled. Ask the Williamson County appraisal district which apply and how a move would change your cap.

sections.h2: When are Georgetown tax bills and protests due?
sections.html:
The statewide property tax calendar governs here. Values are fixed on January 1 and bills arrive near the start of October.

  • Value notices for homesteads begin about April 1.
  • Protests generally close mid-May, or 30 days after the notice if later.
  • Half of a split payment is due November 30, the rest June 30.
  • Late charges begin after January 31.

A dispute can continue past the review board to district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values over $1,000,000. The Comptroller also notes that an appealing owner generally has to pay the undisputed part before the delinquency date.

sections.h2: What should I prepare before listing or accepting an offer in Georgetown?
sections.html:
Gather paperwork first, because gaps in documents delay closings more than repairs do. A complete file also lets you compare offers on equal terms, and it speeds up the title company's work once you accept one.

  • The newest tax statement, listing each taxing unit.
  • Payoff letters for every loan, second mortgages and equity lines included.
  • Proof of any homestead, senior or veteran exemption you hold.
  • Permits and receipts for past work, particularly if you live near the older neighborhoods.
  • Signatures required from co-owners or heirs.

Armed with these, request a written cash offer showing price and closing day, and ask an agent for a range drawn from nearby sales. Compare them by what you keep once payoffs and closing charges are paid, not by the headline price alone. A one-page net sheet from the title company makes the comparison plain.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Georgetown house, or title is unclear?
sections.html:
A sale is possible as soon as ownership is documented. An heir who is not on the recorded deed and wants the homestead exemption must give the appraisal district an affidavit of interest, a death certificate and a utility bill.

Real property under a recorded transfer on death deed passes outside probate. The county clerk takes probate filings, small estate affidavits and deed recordings.

Before you meet buyers, collect the death certificate, any will, and lender payoff statements.

faqs.q: Does Georgetown's growth help a quick sale?
faqs.a: Demand is supported by rapid growth: the Census Bureau estimates 106,907 residents for 2025. Your own house, price and condition decide how fast it sells, so compare offers on net proceeds.

faqs.q: What home value does the Census list for Georgetown?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $429,100 for owner-occupied units for 2020 to 2024. Use it only as a backdrop for your own offer or listing estimate.

faqs.q: Can seniors take their school tax ceiling to a new home?
faqs.a: Yes, in proportion, if you buy another Texas homestead. Check with the appraisal district first.

faqs.q: Which county records my Georgetown deed?
faqs.a: Williamson County, which has its seat at Georgetown. Deeds are filed with that county's clerk.

faqs.q: Do historic rules reach a newer Georgetown house?
faqs.a: Only if your address falls inside one. Ask the city planning office, and keep permit records for any exterior work.
